source_refs.note: Topic 5.2.2 as printed (PDF 128-129, printed 125-126); book error marked: mean printed 75.5 (the scores add to 758, mean 75.8).

blocks.text: Descriptive statistics are used to summarize and organize data. Instead of looking at every individual piece of data, descriptive statistics give us a way to see the overall picture.
Example: Imagine a group of 10 college students takes a math exam, and their scores are: 50, 65, 75, 80, 85, 90, 95, 60, 70, and 88.

items: Mean (Average): The mean score is calculated by adding all the scores and dividing by the number of students.
Highest and Lowest Scores: The highest score is 95, and the lowest score is 50.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The ten scores add up to 758, so the mean is 758/10 = 75.8, not 75.5.
These simple calculations give us a quick summary of how the students performed, without needing to look at each individual score in detail.
